name: regina
author: grids-agent
description: MEDIUM. An n x n board (n = 6, 7 or 8) of '.' and 'X' (blocked squares). The answer is a string of n decimal digits where digit i is the ROW of the queen placed in COLUMN i: n non-attacking queens (no shared row, no shared diagonal - columns are automatic), none of them on a blocked square. The generator first draws a random valid queen configuration and only then sprinkles blocked squares on cells it does not use, so a solution always exists. Discovery path: the demo gives (board, n digits). The digits are always a permutation of 0..n-1, which screams 'one per column, one per row'. From there 'X means forbidden' and 'diagonals too' are the two remaining hypotheses, and each is cheap to test in one round. Partial gradient: a bot that gets rows-only correct scores 0, but a bot that adds diagonals scores 1 on the boards whose blocked squares happen not to bite, so the score climbs in stages.
